policies.title: Chile: named ordinary passports exempt from transient-stay visa
policies.summary: Chile’s current consular transient-stay schedule expressly marks these named nationality rows “NO” under whether a transient-stay visa is required. This is a visa-free short-visitor baseline, not an ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The current schedule directly assigns these nationality rows “NO” under the column asking whether a transient-stay visa is required; it is not an inferred complement.
The schedule’s maximum stay and any note vary by nationality. This candidate records only the ordinary-passport short-visitor access status and does not impose a uniform duration.
The Tourist Card is issued by PDI to people who have already entered as tourists; it is not an ETA, eVisa or visa on arrival.
Residence, third-country-visa, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, territory, special-document and final-admission cases are excluded.

policies.title: Chile: named ordinary passports require advance transient-stay visa
policies.summary: Chile’s current consular transient-stay schedule expressly marks these named nationality rows “SI” under whether a transient-stay visa is required. The authoritative process says a prior authorization or visa is granted by Chilean consulates, so the normalized baseline is visa_required rather than eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: The current schedule directly assigns these nationality rows “SI” under the column asking whether a transient-stay visa is required; it is not an inferred complement.
Chile’s authority describes the authorization or visa as granted by a Chilean consulate. Submitting material through the consular platform does not by itself make the route an eVisa.
The schedule’s conditional exemptions for specified holders of foreign visas, Green Cards or permanent residence are not used to change a passport-wide baseline.

No nationality-wide visa-on-arrival, ETA or eVisa route is established by the cited schedule. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, territory, special-document and final-admission cases are excluded.
